import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Number of squares $\bmod n$

The number of squares modulo $n$.
This is the cardinality of the set $\{k^2 \bmod n \mid k \in \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}\}$.

*References:*
- [A000224](https://oeis.org/A000224)
-/

namespace OeisA224

/-- The number of squares modulo $n$. -/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  if n = 0 then 1
  else
    Finset.card ((Finset.range n).image (fun k : ℕ => k ^ 2 % n))

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 0. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 1. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 2. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 2 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 3. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 2 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 4. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 2 := by decide

/--
$n^2 \equiv 1 \pmod{a(n)(a(n)-1)}$ if and only if $n$ is an odd prime.
- Thomas Ordowski, Jun 08 2017
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) :
    (n.Prime ∧ n ≠ 2) ↔ n ^ 2 ≡ 1 [MOD a n * (a n - 1)] := by
  sorry

end OeisA224

findings.description: The docstring attributes the conjecture to “Thomas Ordowski, Jun 08 2017”, but the cited OEIS entry dates this exact conjecture April 13, 2025. This is a reference-date error; the mathematical statement matches the source.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A000224, COMMENTS, reads: “Conjecture: n^2 == 1 (mod a(n)*(a(n)-1)) if and only if n is an odd prime. - Thomas Ordowski, Apr 13 2025”. Read through the official export at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A000/A000224.seq; the same attribution appears in its April 27, 2025 snapshot.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace “Jun 08 2017” with “Apr 13 2025” in the conjecture docstring.

reformulations.difference: Lean explicitly restricts to n > 1, whereas the OEIS comment leaves the valid-modulus domain implicit. It also expresses “odd prime” as n.Prime ∧ n ≠ 2.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n > 1, the distinct residues 0 and 1 are squares, so a(n) ≥ 2. Since a(1) = 1, the source's modulus a(n)(a(n)−1) is positive on its positive-index domain exactly when n > 1. Thus the restriction implements the ordinary positive-modulus reading, rather than adding Lean's exceptional congruence-modulo-zero case at n = 1. Natural subtraction agrees with integer subtraction on this domain. A prime is odd exactly when it is not 2. In scratch.lean, source_form_iff proves the full equivalence between the Lean statement and the source-order odd-prime formulation quantified over positive moduli.

sources_consulted: Steven Finch and Pascal Sebah, Squares and Cubes Modulo n, March 25, 2016 version, introduction and §1.8; LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/0604465
review.notes: All seven declarations were checked; no substantive mathematical misformalization was found. OEIS has offset 1, so a(0)=1 is a harmless extension outside the source's domain and is unused by the conjecture. The positive-index tests match OEIS. Lean computations found no conjecture mismatch for 2 ≤ n ≤ 300; independent square-count computations matched all 10,000 OEIS table entries and found no conjecture counterexample there. Scratch proofs establish the modulus bounds and statement equivalences without sorryAx. OEIS still labels the statement a conjecture and records verification through 10^8, consistent with research open. The main OEIS webpage returned a browser challenge, so its complete official data export was used. Experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean; the reviewed file remains byte-identical to the specified commit.
